knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A soft spot must be removed and replaced with compacted base in layers. Bedding over it leads to settlement and a dip in the finished surface.
Wet cutting or approved extraction controls silica dust at source. Dry-cutting and dry-sweeping spread respirable dust.
Base depth, cutting, edging, waste and access each drive cost, so they are priced separately rather than as a flat rate.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied mock excavation, the learner builds a base in layers, checks the depth and compaction at each layer and records the results within the assessor's set time.
The learner lays three supplied mock pavers on a bedding layer, checks each with a straightedge and corrects any lip before joints are filled.
The learner performs a wet-cut on a supplied mock paver using the approved control, and cleans up the slurry without dry sweeping.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Base depth and compaction record for the mock excavation, signed by the assessor.
Level check record for the mock pavers.
Assessor observation record of the cutting and clean-up.
stopWorkCriteria: Dry-cutting a mock paver during the assessment.
Operating a plate compactor without hearing protection during the assessment.
Continuing to lay pavers over a mock soft spot that the assessor has identified.
